title: COSHH — Safe Use of Chemicals
blurb: Using cleaning chemicals safely: never mix, follow the label, wear PPE, store properly and act on spills.
siteNotes: Where the COSHH assessments and safety data sheets are kept (your manager will show you).
Which products the venue has approved for each job, and the correct dilutions.
Where the PPE is kept, and where the eyewash and first aid kit are.
legalNotes: COSHH stands for the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health Regulations 2002: employers must assess risks, control exposure, give information and training. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2002/2677
Mixing bleach with an acidic cleaner can release chlorine gas: well-established HSE and manufacturer safety advice.

cards.title: COSHH: Safe Use of Chemicals
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- say what COSHH is and why it matters
- use, wear and store chemicals safely
- act on spills, splashes and unlabelled containers

cards.title: Helpful when right, harmful when wrong
cards.body:
We use cleaning chemicals all day, every day: sanitisers, degreasers, descalers, glasswash detergent. Some of them are genuinely hazardous.

COSHH stands for the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health, and it is the law that makes sure we use them safely. Get it wrong and they can burn skin, damage eyes or release toxic fumes.

items.title: Toxic fumes
items.text: Mixing products is the classic cause.

cards.title: Never mix chemicals
cards.body:
Never mix chemicals. Mixing bleach with an acidic cleaner, for example, can release toxic chlorine gas that can seriously harm you in seconds.

Only use approved products for the job, and follow the label and the COSHH assessment for the right dilution and method.

right.title: Do not
items: Mix bleach with an acidic cleaner

cards.title: PPE, ventilation and storage
cards.body:
Wear the PPE that is provided, usually gloves, and eye protection for stronger products. Make sure there is decent ventilation.

Store chemicals labelled, in their original containers, and well away from food. NEVER decant a chemical into a drinks bottle or an unlabelled container. People have been seriously poisoned that way.

cards.title: Act straight away
cards.body:
If there is a spill, a splash to the skin or eyes, or you feel unwell, act straight away: rinse, get first aid, and report it.

The COSHH information and safety data sheets should be easy to find for everyone who needs them. If you come across an unlabelled container, do not use it and do not guess what is in it. Report it.

items.title: Rinse
items.text: For a splash on skin or eyes.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Never mix chemicals
- Follow the label and the COSHH assessment, and use approved products
- Wear the PPE provided and keep the area ventilated
- Keep chemicals labelled, in original containers, away from food, and never decant into a drinks bottle
- Spill, splash or feel unwell: rinse, get first aid and report. Report unlabelled containers

Control of Safety and Hygiene in Housekeeping
Control of Substances Hazardous to Health
Cleaning Operations for Staff Health and Hygiene
cards.why: COSHH is the Control of Substances Hazardous to Health, the law that makes sure we use these products safely.

cards.q: Mixing bleach with an acidic cleaner can release toxic gas.
cards.why: It can release toxic chlorine gas that can seriously harm you in seconds.

cards.q: Before using a chemical you should follow the label and the...
options: COSHH assessment
Weather forecast
Daily menu
Staff rota
cards.why: Follow the label and the COSHH assessment for the right dilution and method.

cards.q: It's fine to pour a cleaning chemical into an empty drinks bottle to save space.
cards.why: Never decant a chemical into a drinks bottle or unlabelled container. People have been seriously poisoned that way.

cards.q: Which is typical PPE for chemical use?
options: Sunglasses or a peaked cap
Gloves and eye protection
A woollen hat and scarf
A paper apron with no gloves
cards.why: Wear the PPE provided, usually gloves, and eye protection for stronger products.

cards.q: Chemicals should be stored in their original, labelled containers away from food.
cards.why: Store chemicals labelled, in their original containers, and well away from food.

cards.q: You find an unlabelled container of liquid. What should you do?
options: Sniff it to find out what it is
Try it on a small patch
Do not use it or guess, report it
Pour it down the drain
cards.why: Do not use it and do not guess what is in it. Report it.

options: For safety and effectiveness
For the colour of the liquid
For the smell in the room
For the speed of drying
cards.why: Follow the label and the COSHH assessment for the right dilution so the product is safe and works properly.

cards.q: Good ventilation is important when using chemicals.
cards.why: Make sure there is decent ventilation when you use chemicals.

cards.q: What should you do immediately if a chemical splashes your skin or eyes?
options: Wipe it dry and carry on
Wait to see if it stings
Finish the job first
Rinse it off straight away
cards.why: Act straight away: rinse, get first aid, and report it.
